utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm very sorry about the delay this afternoon. So Madam Registrar, would you please talk to the Court deputy of the Milosevic case and ask her to talk to Judge May to finish their case as punctually as possible so that we have no possible delay for the afternoon sitting? It is the intention of this Trial Chamber to finish the testimony of that witness today. So Mr. Krsnik, you have 30 minutes to go with this witness. Could we bring in the witness, please? [The witness entered court].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: [Witness answered through interpreter].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, you may proceed. I think we were at the Heliodrom yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like the technical service to put down the ELMO because I can't see my witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: As you heard yesterday, we have only half an hour, so please concentrate so that we can go through the remaining part of your testimony. Let me remind you we broke off yesterday as Mr. President has already said at the Heliodrom, but yesterday, your last sentence was the SDK, the 4th elementary school, the Jablanica museum, Konjic and Bugojno. This is what you were saying. Can you explain to the Trial Chamber what these locations are, what the ideas of your party were regarding these detention camps and can you just specify what did you mean by these locations?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I think that it's nothing else but tu quoque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we haven't heard anything from this witness yet, and I believe the question asked by Defence counsel is just for some background information. You may answer that question, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness doesn't seem to have the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you hear them now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't hear the Croatian interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can you hear me? Yes. Would you please answer that question, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question of the Trial Chamber or -- ?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, no, my last question, if you can answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really sorry but it takes quite a long time to fix everything. The declaration of the Muslim Democratic Party was a universal declaration of humanitarian character, whose aim was to support the disbanding of all the detention camps, both Croat and Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, it seems to me that the witness is not answering the question. He begins with some declaration --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe the witness is going to answer that question, and the question is tell us something about the Heliodrom, the 4th elementary school, the Jablanica museum, Konjic and Bugojno. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. At the Heliodrom, Muslims were detained by the investigators and police and the military. In the 4th elementary school, the BH Army held Croats in detention. And in the Jablanica museum, which used to be the Tito memorial museum, the Bosnia and Herzegovina organs held in detention Croats. And the same thing went for Bugojno. I think that's the answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now I would like you to look at Exhibit D1/198. Can we please check whether this is the declaration and whether the goal of the declaration was to release -- before that, you didn't mention to the Trial Chamber about the SDK building and the 4th elementary school. Where were these buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ND [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the eastern side of the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were these Croats that were detained there civilians or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, they were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is that the declaration you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber what's the date of the declaration, where, when you wrote it, and whether anyone was released pursuant to this declaration, who you talked to about these matters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The declaration was written by the people in the MDS or people close to the MDS. I have to say again there was this universal humanitarian goal of disbanding all the camps or centres as they were called, and to remove this burden from the relationship between Muslims and Croats. The reason why it was written was to offer the interim authorities of Herceg-Bosna and to the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the international community, to offer this solution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The HZ HB organs, how did they react to this idea when you proposed it to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ND [Resumed]
utterances.text: They read, as far as I know, because I was in Zagreb on some other business at the time because we had to get in touch with the embassies located in Zagreb, because there was a possibility that this might be offered to the embassies of it Turkey, Iran, Germany and also to some relevant authorities in the Republic of Croatia, but president Pohara took this declaration to the then president of Herceg-Bosna, Mr. Boban, and they got in touch with these people in Mostar and they even started with some activities, in an attempt to implement these goals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know whether the HZ HB authorities allowed access to the Heliodrom and that people were released pursuant to this declaration?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the basis of what the people reported to us when they got back, they were able to enter, with the approval of the HZ HB authorities, to Heliodrom and with some offices and investigation centres, they were able to achieve the release of the people who were not under military obligation, who were not conscripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you get in contact with the BH Army organs and what were their reactions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that we got in touch with the organs of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Attempts were made by the people in Mostar through some satellite links. They tried to get in touch with Sarajevo but as these friends of mine informed me, there was no response.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, did you personally, or your party, go to the -- to Mr. Klaus Kinkel, the foreign Minister of Germany, and what was his response to this declaration?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these were the activities that we undertook at the time because our goal was to engage as many members of the international community as possible, and I believe that we did get in touch, and that Mr. Pohara, Mr. Hadziosmanovic, who was in Mostar throughout this whole time period, and he went to visit the detainees with Mr. Pohara, they went to Germany, I think that Mr. Baksic, the President of the Croatian Muslim democratic party from Zagreb, also went there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ND [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted] Please I would like to request that we go into private session now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, did you know, Vinko Martinovic in 1992, 1993, his nickname was Stela?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours I've heard about Mr. Martinovic but as I was told, so this is something that I heard, I do not know him, and what heard was that he was a member of the earliest formations engaged in the liberation of Mostar. Those forces were called HOS, and subsequently, he joined the regular HVO forces. That is all I know. That is I've heard about him but I do not know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know what role he played during the conflict between the BH Army and the Croat Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Perhaps you will give us a couple of minutes just to distribute our exhibits in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: The booths already have the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will start begging here. Must it be one minute before the cross-examination that we get the documents? And look at them. Look at the bundle. Haven't we agreed that we would be getting those documents after the witness had been sworn in? So that the defence can get ready? This is really an ambush. One minute before. The Chamber decided that it would be immediately after the witness has made a solemn declaration and it was at your request, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, as far as I remember, there was no such -- even gentlemen agreement on providing the documents to the defence just after the oath has been taken by the witness. Nor was there any written decision on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, Mr. Seric? I saw you're still standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. I was just expecting a copy of the documents for us. That is the only reason. Thank you. I've just got it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have debated this issue already, and this Trial Chamber made a decision concerning of the motion filed by the Defence counsel. In cross-examination, it is the nature of the surprising attack. That's the purpose of the cross-examination. And if the Prosecution could distribute this bundle of documents during the break, that will save us a lot of time during the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Your Honour, we didn't have any break today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my apologies but for the transcript, I wish to say that the Defence was not treated in this manner. I put it to you that we were not treated in this manner at the time when we conducted the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you may proceed, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Excuse me but for the sake of your safety, I will call you Mr. ND sometimes, so don't get offended, please, because witness sometimes sounds very official. Is it all right with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I will start my cross-examination just with some pieces of Mr. Krsnik's last topic. That's about Heliodrom and another trial where the witness took part. First of all about Heliodrom, Witness, is it correct that you have just told the Trial Chamber that it was Heliodrom was a sort of military investigative body? Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did say that it was an area. I said it's very difficult for me to call it a camp or detention centre. That was a place where military investigations were conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you mean, then, to say that this famous declaration was distributed by your party among people, prisoners, who were being investigated as suspects or accused? Because they were kept in the investigative centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that people were taken there by military investigating authorities who were to investigate whether they were members of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, of ABiH units.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: But I suggest that you know that if a person is under investigation, they should be some warrant of arrest or detention by the Prosecutor or by the Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: A technical problem, this microphone in front of my client is on and he's having a hard time listening to the testimony. Could someone from the technical booth turn it off?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe someone from the technical booth could help us. Don't do it by yourself. Is it off? Is that okay? Let's try it. Well, maybe during the break, it could be fixed. Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Mr. ND, is it normal that representatives of your party were meddling with investigative issues of the authorities whom you considered lawful?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, may I answer, but just let me just ask you a question if I may, of course, if that is all right under the Court practice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's the practice before this Tribunal that you should only answer the question. If you don't understand the question, you may ask for some clarifications, but generally speaking, you should answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We thought that for humane reasons, it would be proper to engage in political activity, because that perhaps would calm down the passions. On the 19th of May, Izetbegovic and Tudjman were in Medjugorje. What was done? Nothing. So we had to do something. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, I didn't ask you about negotiations between Tudjman, Izetbegovic. My question was quite clear-cut.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ND [Resumed]
utterances.text: We thought that it would be good for us to try to do something at a political level to undertake a political -- undertake political steps to, and that is why I said Heliodrom and the SDK, that is all the places where there were some detained, either by the authorities of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO. This was a universal humanitarian declaration. A political declaration.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: The main value, I think of any judicial activity is independence of judicial authorities, is it correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why, yes. I am a very legalistically minded. That is why I came here. I believe in the independence and fairness of this Tribunal. And I think that this is the key to the establishment of lasting peace in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you still believe that there were no civilians in Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That there were no civilians? Why, there were those civilians but they were released. There were the military investigators and they questioned them and let the civilians go.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you mean that there were no civilians in July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, yes, there were some civilians, and the declaration was intended to have them freed, but they -- this existed on both sides. I mean the declaration is universal. It does not apply to the Heliodrom only, but there were some -- some results from achieved at the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you. We will proceed with the Heliodrom a little bit later. And now, Your Honours, I would like you to it allow us to go into session for some minutes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yesterday, during your testimony and today, you also said that there was no discrimination, you never heard or saw any acts of discrimination, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see my transcript, but as far as I can remember since yesterday, yes, I still stand by that opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, did you know a Mr. Tadic from the HVO government?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this be struck out, please? Or to go back into private session once again? That is one thing. And secondly, Witness, do not answer until you've seen the Prosecutor switch off his microphone because if these microphones are not switched off, then your voice can get through. But can this please either be redacted or we have to go back into private session because it is very easy to know who could be a member of the Herceg-Bosna's government.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I didn't expect the witness to just talk about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll go back to the private session for a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 7.09 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 8th day of May, 2002, at 2.15 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25
